results.title: Bob.svg
results.desc: This man was a United States Army infantry soldier during the Mexican Expedition in the World War I era. I do not know what his name was. I call him Bob. This image was created (with substantial alterations) from a photograph taken by C. Tucker Beckett , another infantryman, at night while they and their fellows of Company A, 16th Infantry Regiment were seated around a bonfire. The Regiment was encamped at San Jerónimo , Chihuahua , Mexico , and the photo was taken May 27th, 1916 . Beckett wrote an interesting narrative article in a contemporary photography magazine that is available via Google Books at the time of this writing: Beckett, C. Tucker (1916-11). " Military Photography in Mexico ". The Camera: A Practical Magazine for Photographers 20 (11): pp. 599-616. This is a relatively large SVG image and it should scale to several times the resolution of the original scanned image with limited degredation. It was created using the open source software tools Autotrace , Paint.NET , GIMP , Scribus , and Inkscape .

results.title: Deep Crux wide field with fog.jpg
results.desc: Wide field photo of the Crux (Southern Cross) constellation. The Coalsack Dark Nebula can be seen as the dark area below-right in the constellation. This photo was taken under foggy skies, causing the stars to become large glowing orbs. Image was created using 15 × 182 second (45 mins total) sub exposures taken with a stock Canon EOS 5D Mark II and 100 mm f/2.8L IS Macro lens at f/4 and ISO 1600 mounted on an Astrotrac equatorial mount, stacked using Deep Sky Stacker and finished using Adobe Photoshop CS5.
